bull_bear.body:
- Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise status with over 100 years of operations in India
- 3rd largest retail network in India with 25,098 retail outlets, 1,353 commissioned during the year
- 2nd largest LPG marketer in India; HP Gas achieved its highest-ever dispatch of 9.41 MMT, up 5.2% year-on-year
- India's largest lube refinery and leading marketer of industrial and automotive lubricants
- 2nd largest cross-country product pipeline network at 5,440 km, giving low-cost evacuation and supply-chain reach
- Crude sourcing flexibility - 10 new grades added during the year taking the crude basket to 188 grades from West Africa, Middle East, North America, South America, Mediterranean, North Sea, Far East, Russia and India
- Advanced R&D infrastructure with a cumulative patent portfolio filed and granted
- Technology leadership in residue upgradation - the world's first and largest LC-Max unit at Visakh Refinery enabling 93% conversion of bottom-of-the-barrel residues into high-value distillates
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Crude oil price volatility and geopolitical supply shock — Dated Brent opened FY 2025-26 at US$ 67.7 per barrel and averaged US$ 70.3, but a March 2026 military escalation in West Asia sent prices briefly toward US$ 130 per barrel with Dubai touching US$ 169; the Board notes these geopolitical developments 'are bound to have a pronounced impact on the Corporation, in the near future.'
- Strait of Hormuz chokepoint dependence — The Strait handles approximately 20% of global oil trade and is the critical transit point for the high-sulphur grades that dominate the Indian crude basket; its effective closure in March 2026 produced a supply shock that pushed the Indian basket to a monthly average of US$ 113.5 per barrel.
- Refining margin cyclicality — Singapore complex refining margins swung from US$ 3.8 per barrel in Q2 FY 2025-26 to US$ 8.78 per barrel in Q4; annual profitability depended heavily on a back-loaded spike in middle distillate cracks rather than a broad-based margin environment.
- Concentration of margin in middle distillates — The annual strength was driven by the substantial widening of middle distillate cracks in Q3 and Q4, with Gasoil margins climbing to US$ 24.5 per barrel in Q3; 'the sharp spike in Gasoil margins toward the end of the year, triggered by supply shock concerns, ensured that overall refinery profitability remained robust', leaving earnings exposed if the diesel crack normalises.
- Structurally weak naphtha and fuel oil cracks — Naphtha margins were the weakest segment through the year, at US$ -4.6 per barrel in Q1 and US$ -6.8 per barrel in Q2 on a sluggish petrochemical complex and a shift toward alternative feedstocks, while High Sulphur Fuel Oil 180 CST margins corrected to US$ -5.5 per barrel in Q2 and US$ -7.0 per barrel in Q3.
- Demand headwinds from trade policy and a projected global oil surplus — U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports and forecasts of a significant global oil surplus in early 2026 dampened demand expectations and pressured prices through Q3, and rising non-OPEC+ output from the United States and Brazil capped prices for most of the year.
- Crude sourcing and supply-chain execution risk — Maintaining throughput through the March 2026 disruption required robust crude planning and agile supply chain management; the Corporation mitigates this by processing new opportunity crudes - 10 new grades processed for the first time, taking the basket to 188 grades across nine sourcing regions including Russia.
- Large-project execution and ramp risk in refinery upgradation — The Corporation is dependent on modernization and expansion of its refineries to meet growing domestic demand; the LC-Max Residue Upgradation Facility at Visakh and the Mumbai Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project must deliver designed conversion and yield to realise the intended value uplift.

business.body: HPCL refines crude oil at its Mumbai and Visakhapatnam refineries and markets petroleum products nationwide through an extensive infrastructure network spanning retail outlets, LPG distribution, lubricants, aviation fuels, pipelines and natural gas. It is India's leading marketer of industrial and automotive lubricants and serves retail motorists, households, aviation customers and direct industrial and commercial buyers across India. The Corporation is diversifying beyond conventional fuels through investments in natural gas, biofuels, green hydrogen, electric mobility and renewable energy, guided by a Net Zero 2040 commitment.

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the core refining and marketing business while building a more resilient, diversified and future-ready energy portfolio
- Aggressively diversify the crude supply chain - 10 new grades integrated during the year taking the portfolio to 188 crude grades - and diversify LPG procurement away from a single region through spot purchases outside Gulf countries
- Supply optimisation through nil imports of MS/HSD, strategic sourcing from domestic refineries, cost takeout initiatives and improved coastal and rail logistics
- Project Samriddhi, the Corporation's EBITDA improvement programme, targeting cost optimisation, operational excellence and margin enhancement
- Strengthen the balance sheet through prudent capital allocation and disciplined cost management to withstand market volatility
- Refining excellence and bottom-of-the-barrel upgradation, anchored by the LC-MAX Residue Upgradation Facility at Visakh Refinery
- Digital and advanced process optimisation across refineries - Advanced Process Control in all VRMP units, Real Time Optimiser across Mumbai and Visakh Refinery units, and DigiSuite analytics on the RUF
- Complete and ramp HRRL as one of India's most advanced integrated refinery and petrochemical complexes to strengthen the downstream portfolio
- Continued investment in pipelines, LPG bottling plants, terminals, depots, biofuels, logistics infrastructure and renewables
- Expand the retail network alongside non-fuel retailing and digital customer engagement platforms
- Build the gas and alternate energy ecosystem across LNG, City Gas Distribution and gas marketing, plus EV charging and CNG-enabled outlets
- Innovation and research-led growth through patent filing, startup collaboration across the oil and gas value chain, and adoption of AI, advanced analytics, machine learning and predictive maintenance
- Digital transformation treated as a business transformation programme to enhance agility, efficiency and customer-centricity
- As a Government Company and Maharatna CPSE, HPCL's capital allocation is exercised under a Board framework of well-developed internal controls, an Empowerment and Authority Manual and a Procurement Manual, with oversight by external authorities including the C&AG, the Central Vigilance Commission and Parliamentary Committees. The Board maintains a Project Evaluation and Review Committee to appraise investment proposals, alongside Audit and Risk Management Committees. Distribution practice is to pay an interim dividend during the year and place the final dividend before Members for declaration at the Annual General Meeting, with the interim payment confirmed at the same meeting. The stated intent is to protect and enhance stakeholder value through strategic supervision while reinvesting in the business.
- Net Zero for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2040 - 'Your Corporation is slated to be a Net zero company for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2040'
- Enhancing energy efficiency identified as one of the major levers for achieving the net zero targets, pursued through process optimization, advanced control systems, energy recovery, equipment upgrades, renewable energy integration and employee engagement
- Reducing the environmental footprint of refining operations through modernization and expansion projects, alongside the national priorities of energy accessibility, affordability, security and sustainability
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: HPCL's expansion programme in FY 2025-26 spanned refining upgradation, pipelines, terminals, gas infrastructure and marketing network build-out. In refining, the Corporation commissioned the Residue Upgradation Facility (RUF) at Visakh Refinery in December 2025, featuring the world's first and largest LC-Max unit with a capacity of 3.55 MMTPA and enabling 93% conversion of bottom-of-the-barrel residues into high-value distillates, supported by a "DigiSuite" real-time process and equipment analytics layer. At Mumbai Refinery, the Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project is under execution to raise LOBS production from the current 475 KTPA to 764 KTPA. In pipelines, the 90 km Bhatinda-Sangrur Multiproduct Pipeline (BSPL) was commissioned to enhance evacuation of white oil products from Guru Gobind Singh Refinery (HMEL) at Ramanmandi, and the 216 km Barmer-Palanpur Multiproduct Pipeline (BPPL) was commissioned with HSD pumped to enable the commissioning of HRRL. The Crude Oil Terminal at Mundra was commissioned with 12 tanks of 720 TKL total capacity, with the first crude vessel unloaded and vessel loading facilities commissioned; the 493 km AMPL crude pipeline from Mundra to HRRL Refinery, Pachpadra, and the 74 km MCPL crude pipeline from Cairn Barmer to HRRL were also commissioned. On the forward expansion front, the 201 km Haldia-Panagarh LPG Pipeline is nearing completion to serve LPG demand in West Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand, and the 540 km Visakh-Raipur Pipeline is progressing across Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. In gas, the CGD network added 3 new City Gate Stations (total 14), 8 Mother Stations (total 24), 55 CNG stations (total 530) and 47,216 new domestic PNG connections, while 2 new LNG retail stations were commissioned (total 3) and term LNG contracts were secured to provide base-load support for the newly commissioned Chhara LNG regasification terminal. Petrochemicals readiness is being built ahead of HRRL's 2.4 MMTPA petrochemical capacity coming on stream, including channel-partner readiness for the HP Durapol polymer brand and an investors' meet in Jodhpur for downstream petrochemicals development around the Balotra refinery. In aviation, the network footprint increased to 59 Aviation Service Facilities with new facilities at Dinjan Airforce Station (Tinsukia, Assam) and the civil airports of Solapur and Navi Mumbai, and Mechanical Completion was achieved for the Aviation Fuel Farm at the upcoming Visakhapatnam International Airport (Bhogapuram) with an integrated fuel hydrant system. Supplies and distribution added 1.87 MWp of new solar capacity (total installed 13.47 MWp, meeting nearly 25% of POL energy requirements) across a network of 80 terminals and depots, and Direct Sales hired 35 TMT of storage capacity at Chennai (FO 28 TMT, Bitumen 7 TMT).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global output grew 3.4% in CY 2025 and is projected to moderate to 3.1% in CY 2026, with headwinds from shifting trade policies tempered by rising technology investment
- Global headline inflation declined to 4.1% in CY 2025 and is projected at 4.4% in CY 2026, with upside risk from the escalating conflict in West Asia
- India's provisional real GDP growth of 7.7% in FY 2025-26 makes it the world's fastest-growing major economy, and India ranks as the world's 3rd largest consumer of oil and primary energy
- Indian energy demand grew only 1.1% in CY 2025 and oil demand growth slowed to 0.6%, as biofuel use in road transport rose about 50% and a strong monsoon reduced transport activity
- LPG, mainly for clean cooking, was the main driver of increased Indian oil product demand, supported by government initiatives for rural households
- India's natural gas consumption fell 3.5% in CY 2025 with gas-for-power demand down nearly 10% on robust renewables growth and milder weather
- Renewable electricity generation in India grew 20% in CY 2025 with annual renewable capacity additions up almost 60%, the fastest among major markets
- Dated Brent averaged US$ 70.3 per barrel over FY 2025-26 with extreme Q4 volatility; the March 2026 West Asia escalation closed the Strait of Hormuz (approximately 20% of global oil trade) and drove prices briefly toward US$ 130 per barrel
- The Indian crude oil basket averaged US$ 71.0 per barrel for the year but reached a monthly average of US$ 113.5 per barrel in March 2026 as high-sulphur grades that dominate the basket were disrupted
- Singapore benchmark refining margins improved to an average US$ 6.3 per barrel for FY 2025-26, driven by substantial widening of middle distillate cracks in Q3 and Q4 on winter heating demand and geopolitical risk premium
- Persistent weakness in Naphtha margins from a sluggish petrochemical complex and a shift toward alternative feedstocks, and a mid-year correction in Fuel Oil, partially offset middle-distillate strength
- HPCL capacity utilisation stood at 106.3% and Gross Refining Margin at US$ 8.79 per barrel for the year, reflecting refining as one of the strongest pillars of value creation
- Marketing demand supported by an expanding distribution network - retail sales 30.83 MMT, LPG sales 9.41 MMT, Aviation 1.16 MMT, Lubricants 686 TMT
- Natural gas expected to play a critical role in India's evolving energy mix; HPCL's natural gas portfolio expanded to 624 TMT and CGD sales (CNG+PNG) reached 149 TMT

deepdive.thesis: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited is India's second-largest public sector oil refiner and marketer, operating an extensive retail network to supply transportation fuels, lubricants, and emerging clean energy solutions while driving the nation's energy transition toward net zero by 2040.

open.item: HPCL is slated to become a Net Zero company for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2040, with energy efficiency as a major lever.
Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project at Mumbai Refinery to increase LOBS production from the current 475 KTPA to 764 KTPA.
The same Mumbai Refinery Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project will increase bitumen production by approximately 487 KTPA.

Progressive commissioning of the 9 MMTPA integrated grassroot Refinery-cum-Petrochemical project at Balotra, Rajasthan (HRRL) is in progress, with crude taken in CDU/VDU enabling sequential commissioning of secondary units.
Once fully operational, HRRL will be one of India's most advanced integrated refinery and petrochemical complexes and will significantly strengthen HPCL's downstream portfolio.

As the Residue Upgradation Facility at Visakh Refinery advances through stabilisation towards its designed operating performance, it will transform 93% of bottom-of-the-barrel residue and improve product value realisation.
Management flagged heightened geopolitical uncertainty and crude market turbulence, including the March 2026 closure of the Strait of Hormuz, as the operating terrain the Corporation must manage.
The 201 km Haldia-Panagarh LPG Pipeline is nearing completion to serve LPG demand in West Bengal, Bihar and Jharkhand.
The 540 km Visakh-Raipur Pipeline is progressing across Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
HRRL's 2.4 MMTPA petrochemical capacity is coming on stream, with HPCL building supply-chain and channel-partner readiness for the upcoming petrochemical volumes under the HP Durapol polymer brand.

The annual strength was driven by the substantial widening of middle distillate cracks in Q3 and Q4, with Gasoil margins climbing to US$ 24.5 per barrel in Q3; 'the sharp spike in Gasoil margins toward the end of the year, triggered by supply shock concerns, ensured that overall refinery profitability remained robust', leaving earnings exposed if the diesel crack normalises.
risks.risk: Concentration of margin in middle distillates

risks.note: Naphtha margins were the weakest segment through the year, at US$ -4.6 per barrel in Q1 and US$ -6.8 per barrel in Q2 on a sluggish petrochemical complex and a shift toward alternative feedstocks, while High Sulphur Fuel Oil 180 CST margins corrected to US$ -5.5 per barrel in Q2 and US$ -7.0 per barrel in Q3.
risks.risk: Structurally weak naphtha and fuel oil cracks

risks.note: U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports and forecasts of a significant global oil surplus in early 2026 dampened demand expectations and pressured prices through Q3, and rising non-OPEC+ output from the United States and Brazil capped prices for most of the year.
risks.risk: Demand headwinds from trade policy and a projected global oil surplus

risks.note: Maintaining throughput through the March 2026 disruption required robust crude planning and agile supply chain management; the Corporation mitigates this by processing new opportunity crudes - 10 new grades processed for the first time, taking the basket to 188 grades across nine sourcing regions including Russia.
risks.risk: Crude sourcing and supply-chain execution risk

risks.note: The Corporation is dependent on modernization and expansion of its refineries to meet growing domestic demand; the LC-Max Residue Upgradation Facility at Visakh and the Mumbai Lube Modernization & Bottom Upgradation Project must deliver designed conversion and yield to realise the intended value uplift.
risks.risk: Large-project execution and ramp risk in refinery upgradation

meta.thesis: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited is India's second-largest public sector oil refiner and marketer, operating an extensive retail network to supply transportation fuels, lubricants, and emerging clean energy solutions while driving the nation's energy transition toward net zero by 2040.
